claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation can accurately capture local mechanical properties of as-synthesized FeNiCrMn HEA.
Nanoindentation can reveal spatial variations in hardness, elastic modulus, and yield strength that bulk mechanical measurements cannot discern.
The as-synthesized FeNiCrMn HEA has demonstrated corrosion resistance.
The intrinsic microscale mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn HEA is largely unexplored.
Nanoindentation will measure load-displacement responses at multiple localized regions of the alloy.
Polished sample surfaces help ensure reliable nanoindentation results.
The alloy has a heterogeneous microstructure containing individual grains and phase boundaries.
Microstructural heterogeneity is expected to cause localized variations in mechanical properties.
Nanoindentation derives hardness, elastic modulus, and yield strength from recorded load-displacement curves.
The high spatial resolution of nanoindentation permits individual microstructural features to be probed.
Bulk mechanical tests average local mechanical responses and can obscure microscale variations.
Nanoindentation will detect significant spatial variations in hardness and elastic modulus in FeNiCrMn HEA.
Stronger phases or grain-boundary regions will display higher hardness and elastic modulus.
Local yield strength will vary relative to values averaged by bulk mechanical tests.
Compression and tensile tests provide mechanical-property values averaged over the material.
Surface-preparation quality can influence nanoindentation results.
Features smaller than the nanoindenter tip resolution may not be measured reliably.
Converting nanoindentation load-displacement data into exact macroscale yield-strength values is uncertain.
Independent bulk testing is necessary to calibrate nanoindentation-derived yield-strength estimates.
The quantitative relationship between nanoindentation responses and bulk properties can vary because of microstructural heterogeneity.
